label: Design 6 - New Bedroom Pod + Bedroom 2 Lounge
summary: An addition-led alternative: build a compact new bedroom where the site works best, turn Bedroom 2 into a better lounge/day room, and avoid forcing the replacement bedroom into the old sunroom shape.
room_changes: A new compact bedroom pod is added in the best available legal and practical location.
The office may become part of a wet/service core if needed.
The current lounge becomes media, snug, guest overflow, or quiet room.
The sunroom is removed, reduced, or converted only if it still earns its place.
The renovated kitchen stays unless minor connection work is needed.
daylight_strategy: Use Bedroom 2 and the back/service side for daily living instead of a low-use bedroom/service mix.
Place the new bedroom so it does not steal the best living light or darken kitchen/dining.
Treat the deck as part of the living system with shade and wind control.
movement_strategy: Strengthen garage/back arrival to kitchen, deck, and the new lounge.
Keep the new bedroom private enough for sleeping rather than placing it in the active deck route.
Use the current lounge as a quieter secondary space after the main living function moves.
build_scope: Construct a new bedroom pod/addition with foundations, envelope, insulation, windows, heating, and finishes.
Alter Bedroom 2, entrance, laundry, and possibly office/bathroom relationships.
Resolve deck circulation and shade around the new addition.
Potentially remove or reduce the sunroom.
risks: Site setbacks, drainage, foundations, roof connection, and consent may drive cost.
A poorly placed pod could damage deck use, garden space, or kitchen/dining light.
This may be more expensive than replacing the sunroom if the sunroom footprint is actually buildable.
Needs professional feasibility before detailed app modelling goes too far.
cost_notes: Broad planning band: NZD 280k to 500k+ depending on addition size, site constraints, services, and envelope complexity.
